title: each Error class in an Action failure channel becomes its own variant under its own durable identity, derived from the declaring module and the class name
notes: specification/failures.mdx:33 (Locked): 'The compiler MUST provide stable nominal identity, matching metadata, serialization evidence, and cross-realm transport metadata while preserving ordinary Error behavior', and :209: 'Handler selection MUST use compiler-stable nominal identity, not a forgeable user _tag or minifier-sensitive constructor name in compiled artifacts.' Read on the durable boundary (specification/durable-execution.mdx: 'Every value crossing an Action or Flow persistence boundary MUST satisfy the compiler-checked durable codec contract'), that makes an identity the key a decoder selects a handler by, and stability is worth nothing without INJECTIVITY: two Error classes arriving under one identity is exactly a forgeable key. Line 2 is that obligation and it is the only line here that can go to '1'. 04-nominal-errors/a-nominal-error-identity-names-its-declaring-module pins the RUNTIME identity spelling through the harness's identity accessor; this case pins the DURABLE contract identity, which is a different string minted by a different normalizer in the same compiler, and until now nothing in the corpus opened it. WHAT THIS CASE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT PIN: the identity's spelling. The reference mints `smithers:<module>_<Name>@1`, and the `_` in it is a normalized `#` — the separator is rewritten by the same pass that normalizes the rest, which is why the durable spelling is NOT injective over (module, class name) in general. Declaring the literal string here would ratify that spelling as the contract and make the one-character repair a corpus break for a reason the specification does not state. So the case observes the three properties the documentation actually names — one variant per class, one identity per variant, and an identity derived from the declaring module and the class's own name — and leaves the separator to whoever owns contract versioning. The unpinnable half of this obligation is recorded in COVERAGE.md as observation gap #15. This case pins CURRENT behaviour on both counts: the identity lane's fix does not change this program (it added a refusal beside the identity, and every benign form was measured byte-identical before and after), so it was not failing before. Its value is that the obligation had no case at all. The Go fork scored `unsupported` here until 2026-08-28, and the reason was measured, not assumed: it emitted the legacy stub error schema, so the descriptor it checks this program against was `{ digest, format, role, schemaVersion, shape, source }` with no `descriptor` field, and `schema.descriptor` reported TS2339 on an authored `.sm` file — the harness's definition of 'parsed Smithers syntax it has no handling for'. That stub is gone: the fork now derives the error schema from the declared failure channel the way `poc/src/durable/schema.ts` does, this case scores `pass` on both backends, and the obligation IS differenced. It differences hard: the two backends were measured to agree byte-for-byte on the whole Plan for this program, including both failure identities, both `errorSchema` digests, the `contractDigest`, and `plan.digest`. Every narrowing failure in `main` prints a distinct sentence rather than an empty line, so no path through this program can satisfy the expectation by observing nothing. Verified load-bearing rather than assumed: mutating the second stdout line from '2' to '1' turns the case red on the reference with the stdout diff printed, and the file was restored byte-identically (sha256 compared before and after).
